text:
maria: Heads up — saw ~3x p50 spike on shared-gpu-c around 02:15 UTC. Correlates with a burst of large-context few-shot requests from tenant @ads-intel. Grafana panels: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/pool-shared-c (private).

infra-bot: ALERT: pool shared-gpu-c high-kernel-switch-rate detected. Autoswitches to int8_kern_v2 between 02:10-02:20 (10 switches/min).

kevin: quick check of agent logs: KV cache eviction rate jumped ~8x for that pool at 02:12. GPU mem pressure + repeated prefix misses. Looks like long prompts are thrashing the per-tenant KV allocation and causing fallback to slower attention kernels.

nidhi: did batching heuristics change? I see a rollout at 02:05 that widened the pack-window to 40ms (release 2026.02.05). Wider window can mix long & short requests -> bad packing for long-context workloads.

sam: repro locally against pool-staging: 10x few-shot seq_len=6k requests from a single tenant causes kernel autoselect to pick slower tiled-attn kernel and KV churn. Collected runtime logs + nvidia-smi snippet:
```
GPU0 Mem: 24000MiB / 24576MiB
KV cache entries oscillating 20k -> 2k every few seconds
runtime: switching kernels: fast_attn_v1 -> tiled_attn_v3
```

sam: also saw large latency tail when batch coalesced short chat requests with one long request in same batch (packing mismatch).

elaine: proposed immediate mitigations:
- add temporary per-tenant token-per-minute cap for shared pools (soft throttle)
- rollback pack-window widening for shared pools to previous 15ms
- pin kernel selection to safe_kern_v1 for the pool until we get a proper profile
- add a KV-reservation path for very large-context requests to avoid evicting others

kevin: I can push an edge rate-limit rule (nginx + rate-limiter) to throttle that tenant to 5k tokens/min on shared pools. Pushing in 5m and will monitor.

kevin: starting a distributed trace + per-tenant KV hit/miss metric collection now (trace id trc_1805554321). Will post results.

maria: thanks. follow-ups: we should schedule a short perf postmortem tomorrow (30m) to decide long-term: per-tenant reservation, adaptive batching by seq_len, or move large-context tenants to Dedicated. i'll file the calendar invite and RFC.

elaine: sample rate-limiter snippet for edge (nginx lua):
```
local tokens = tonumber(ngx.var.http_x_tokens or 0)
if tokens > 5000 then
  return ngx.exit(429)
end
```

nidhi: also add a perf test in CI that mixes short chat + occasional long few-shot to catch regressions in batching changes.

maria: good call. tagging @eng-sre to ensure incident postmortem notes go to incidents channel and we add runbook steps for noisy-large-context tenants. :white_check_mark:
